cards.text: Hezekiah, king of Judah, was sick enough to die, and the LORD added fifteen years to his life (Isaiah 38:1, 5). The news travels all the way to Babylon, where King Merodach-baladan son of Baladan hears about the illness AND the recovery. BABYLON, friend, that's word getting around faster than a rumor in the office group chat.

cards.question: So what does Merodach-baladan, king of Babylon, send to Hezekiah?

cards.text: A get-well card from a KING! The envoys arrive from Babylon, and Hezekiah welcomes them gladly.

cards.question: Hezekiah shows the envoys from Babylon only a few of his treasures.

cards.text: Silver, gold, spices, precious oil, the ENTIRE armory: there's nothing in his palace or in all his dominion that Hezekiah doesn't show them. Friend, that's not a tour, that's handing a stranger your unlocked phone with the banking app already open.
Then the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz (Isaiah 38:1) goes to King Hezekiah and asks where those men came from and what they said. Hezekiah tells him they came from a distant land, from Babylon.
Next Isaiah asks what they've seen. Hezekiah says they've seen everything in his palace: "There is nothing among my treasures that I did not show them."

cards.question: Isaiah brings Hezekiah the word of the LORD of Hosts. The time will surely come when everything in Hezekiah's palace, and all that his fathers stored up, will be what?
It's not just the treasure. The LORD says some of Hezekiah's ___ will be taken away to be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.

cards.text: His own flesh and blood. That's heavy news, and now it's Hezekiah's turn to answer the prophet.

cards.question: What does Hezekiah tell Isaiah about the word of the LORD he just heard?
Hezekiah calls the word of the LORD good. What was he thinking?

answers.text: At least his own lifetime will have peace
Babylon will soon forget all about Judah
Isaiah could still turn out to be mistaken
